changes.text: [rework] Timelines is now built into Notebooks
sub: The + button next to Notebooks now asks Pages or Timeline — Timeline creates a timeline with its own notebook
Selecting a timeline's notebook shows its full epoch/era editor right there — add/reorder epochs, add/delete/move eras, all the same editing the standalone Timelines room has
Every epoch and era gets its own page in that notebook automatically, kept in sync by name in both directions
New notebooks and timelines are named "Notebook 1", "Timeline 1", etc. by default instead of starting blank
Whether "Timeline" is offered as a notebook type is a Preference (Display → Notebooks), off by default — the standalone Timelines room still exists for anyone who wants it separately

changes.text: [new] Duration, status, tags, and linked entries live directly in the page now
sub: Each is a real chip inside the page's own text — duration and tags are click-and-type, status is a dropdown, linked entries are clickable and colored by entry type
A protected properties block at the top keeps these separate from your prose — typing in one can't bleed into the other, in either direction
Editing from the Timelines tab and editing on the page write to the exact same place — there's no longer a separate copy of any of these to drift out of sync
The old separate Summary/Notes fields are gone — the page's own body is the actual writing space now

changes.text: [new] Sort pages by Last edited, A–Z, Chronological, or Timeline order
sub: Timeline order walks a notebook's pages in the same epoch/era sequence they appear in Timelines — only offered for a timeline's own notebook, and is its default sort there
Every other notebook still defaults to Last edited, same as before

changes.text: [new] Epoch/era terminology is configurable
sub: Preferences → Display → Notebooks lets you pick what the bigger and smaller divisions are called — independently of each other, so any combination works, not just matched pairs
Affects the Timelines editor and its embedded copy in Notebooks everywhere — button labels, placeholders, empty states, delete confirmations

changes.text: [removed] Chart and Map views
sub: Timelines is edit-only now, in both the standalone room and the copy embedded in Notebooks
Removed rather than kept around unused — simpler to maintain, and one less thing pulling focus from the actual writing

changes.text: [rework] Pages renamed to Notebooks, and its icon swapped with Entries
sub: Purely a relabel/re-icon — nothing about how notebooks or pages work changed

changes.text: [redesign] Timelines, Entries, and Oracle are now hidden by default
sub: Applies to new projects and the Blank project type — existing projects are untouched
Every built-in project type was re-checked against this: Novel and Worldbuilding still show Entries/Timelines since they need them, Poetry/Product/Screenplay already hid what they don't use
Project types now also control whether "Timeline" is offered as a notebook type, not just what's visible in the sidebar
Switching or picking a project type now shows exactly what it turns on, computed live from the preset rather than hand-written — can't drift out of sync with what the preset actually does
Timelines carries a new "Optional" tag in Preferences, separate from Experimental/Recommended — it's not unfinished, it's just no longer the primary way to use timelines now that Notebooks covers it

changes: [redesign] Preferences toggles are rounded switches now instead of checkboxes
[fix] The Productivity tile in Preferences → Display was full-width for no reason, leaving an empty gap — sized to match Sidebar/Home/Notebooks now

changes.text: [new] Experimental: an onboarding-style layout for the full Preferences menu
sub: Off by default — turn it on in Preferences to try it
Walks through the same settings as a series of focused steps instead of a grid of categories — nothing about what each setting does has changed, just how you move through them

changes.text: [new] Pages can now carry their own tasks
sub: A collapsible Tasks panel sits to the right of the editor — check things off, set an optional due date, and open a full Edit view (title, notes, due-date range, repeat) shared with Productivity's own task editor

These are the same tasks Productivity's Calendar "Tasks" card already tracks, just filtered to one page — check one off from either place and it updates everywhere, including a "No due date" group for tasks that are just a plain to-do
The panel starts expanded on wide screens and collapsed on narrow ones by default; once you toggle it yourself, your choice sticks
Small progress rings on notebooks and pages show how many of their tasks are done, with a hover tooltip — stay hidden entirely until there's actually a task

changes.text: [new] Export a page to HTML or Markdown
sub: New Export button in the page editor opens a print-dialog-style panel: pick the format, what to include (title, notebook & date, tags), and preview it live before saving
HTML export can match your current app theme, or fall back to a plain light layout
Print opens your browser's print dialog directly, always using the plain light layout regardless of the export format chosen

changes.text: [new] Rest token history
sub: A History link next to your rest token count shows every token you've earned or spent, newest first, grouped by month
A week that both hits the weekly goal and clears the overachieve challenge shows as one combined "+2" line instead of two near-identical ones
Entries are dated to when they actually happened — catching up on several missed weeks at once no longer bunches them all under today

A week (for goal/overachieve) or a day (for a spend) can only ever produce one real entry — a repeat is treated as a duplicate check, not a second event, and skipped rather than logged again; existing saves get any already-duplicated entries collapsed down to one automatically
Filter to just Earned or just Spent

Undoing a rest day, or logging work after marking one rested, cancels the original "spent" entry outright instead of adding a separate "refunded" line — keeps the log from cluttering up with pairs that net out to nothing
Existing saves with a token balance already banked get a single "starting balance" entry so the log doesn't start out looking empty

changes: [fix] Renaming a notebook: pressing spacebar partway through typing a multi-word name could exit the rename early, making it hard to type past the first word

changes.text: [fix] Lists in the page editor could get permanently stuck, with no way to press Enter to escape back to plain text
sub: Most noticeable right after importing/converting an old markdown page, where a list is often the very last thing in the document — exactly the case browsers handle least reliably on their own
Pressing Enter on an empty list item (or an empty checklist item) now always exits the list cleanly, splitting it in two if it wasn't at the very end

changes.text: [new] Tables in pages
sub: New Table button in the editor toolbar inserts a starter table; Tab / Shift+Tab move between cells
Tab from the last cell adds a new row and jumps into it, spreadsheet-style, for quickly growing a table as you go
Right-click a cell for a floating quick-menu at the click point — Insert/Delete row, Insert/Delete column, Delete table — matching how Google Docs and most other table editors handle it

Clicking the Table button while the caret is inside an existing table opens the same actions in a modal instead — the one that's always used when a page is popped out into its own window, where a floating menu positioned by click coordinates would show up in the wrong place
Markdown tables (the standard "| col | col |" / "| --- | --- |" format) are now understood on import, and page-to-Markdown export writes them back out the same way
First step toward pages picking up more of what World Entries can do

changes: [fix] The patch notes panel was missing from the shared dialog styling that Update/Onboarding use, so it rendered without sizing, background, or layout — now matches the update-available screen it was always meant to look like

changes.text: [redesign] Oracle is now tagged Experimental instead of Beta
sub: The Beta/Recommended tag system now supports an Experimental tag generally, for anything earlier-stage than Beta — not just Oracle

changes.text: [rework] Management is per-project now; Productivity stays shared across all of them, with a filter to view just one
sub: Budget and products belong to whichever project you're in — a Poetry project and a client-work project no longer share the same wallet

Sessions, plans, weekly goals, streaks, medals, and rest days are still pooled across every project like before — splitting those apart per-project turned out to be more confusing than useful, since nobody wants their weekly goal or streak reset just by switching projects mid-week
New: a project filter on the Sessions list narrows the view down to one project's own hours without changing what counts toward your goal, streak, or medals

Existing saves are migrated automatically: Management's data splits apart by whichever project logged the most sessions (nothing was ever tagged per-project before), and Productivity's data is re-merged back into one shared pool

changes.text: [new] Project types: tell Notebook what a project is for
sub: Six presets to start from — Blank, Novel/Story, Worldbuilding/Campaign, Screenplay, Poetry/Collection, and Product/Professional work — each with sensible defaults for what's visible
Save your own custom presets from any project's current setup, reusable when creating new ones
Picking a type is part of creating a new project now, and can be changed later from Settings

Creating a new Blank project now walks you through onboarding for it, the same setup new installs get — since what's visible is per-project now, this is worth doing for each blank one rather than just the first

changes.text: [new] Two new ways to move between projects
sub: Quick-swap — a "Switch" button in the sidebar, or Ctrl/Cmd+P — jumps straight to another project without sending you to Home first; closing it drops you back on whatever page you were already on

Projects breakdown, from the Projects menu or quick-swap, splits hours and sessions by which project was active when logged (Productivity's own totals are shared, same as always), plus each project's own wallet, products, and page/entry/timeline counts — read-only, without switching into any of them

changes.text: [new] Management overhaul: investments and products got a lot deeper
sub: Investments can now be cashed out — enter what you actually received and only the profit (or loss) beyond your original principal is logged, so a $300 investment cashed out for $350 shows $50 earned, not $350
Cash-outs can be edited afterward, and deleting one reverts the investment to "not yet cashed out" — exactly as if it never happened
Products can log repeatable returns — early returns recoup the product's cost first, and only the excess counts as profit
Products can carry an optional date, which keeps a matching entry on your calendar in sync automatically
Product and transaction notes are no longer shown inline in the list — click a row to view its full details instead

changes.text: [new] Budgets: set spending limits for any timeframe, not just monthly
sub: Add as many budgets as you want — Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly, or a custom date range
Each one can optionally be scoped to a single category, e.g. a "Marketing" budget that only tracks Marketing expenses
Weekly/Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly budgets automatically roll into the current period — no recreating them
A new Breakdown view groups income, expenses, and investments by category with totals and percentages
"Balance" is now labeled "Wallet" to make clear it's your net take-home, not a running transaction total

changes.text: [redesign] Preferences reorganized for clarity
sub: A new "This project" group at the top holds everything scoped to the current project — Project type and Library
Every category is now a full-width row with a real description of what it does, instead of a cramped icon grid with little to no explanation
Home tiles now pull their icon and label directly from the sidebar, so they can't drift out of sync (e.g. a tile silently still saying "Timer" after the room was renamed "Productivity")

changes: [new] Ctrl/Cmd+S now exports a full backup instead of just forcing an immediate autosave

changes.text: [redesign] The update-available screen's "export first" step is more compact
sub: It's a single line now instead of a whole titled section with its own bulleted steps — the patch notes screen's layout is unchanged

changes.text: [fix] Patch notes could fail to show what a version actually changed
sub: Caused by the app's own version number not being bumped to match the published changelog — fixed, and a console warning now flags it early if it happens again

changes: [fix] Budgets and products weren't included in full JSON exports or selective snapshot restores — they are now
[fix] Investments didn't count toward budget spending limits — putting money into an investment is still money leaving your wallet, so it counts against a budget's limit the same as an expense now
[fix] Setting a weekly goal to 0 hours now properly clears it back to "no goal set," instead of silently storing a 0-hour goal that doesn't mean anything

changes.text: [new] Export is now two separate choices: this project, or everything
sub: Ctrl/Cmd+S now always does a full export — every project, plus shared settings and Productivity — instead of just the current project
Preferences → Data offers both: "Export this project" (the old single-project export) and "Export everything" (new, same as Ctrl/Cmd+S)
Import now reads a full export back in too — replaces every project and shared data at once, with its own stronger confirmation since it's the whole workspace, not just one project

changes: [fix] A single-project export's filename is now based on the project's own name, instead of a generic "notebook-export-DATE.json" for every project
[new] Patch notes now support tags, and lines can be broken down into a sub-bullet list — see this entry's format for an example

changes.text: [new] Management: a new sidebar room for real-world budgeting and product tracking, shared across every project like Productivity
sub: Budget: log income and expenses with category, amount, date, and notes — running income/expense/balance summary
Products: track what you're building through a status pipeline (Idea, Planned, Active, Done)
A Management tile on Home shows your current budget balance

changes.text: [new] In-world economy tracking, integrated into Entries
sub: New Product entry type for fictional goods/items
Added a Wealth field to Characters and a Treasury field to Factions

changes.text: [fix] Rest tokens were accumulating far too fast
sub: New rate: 1 token for hitting your weekly goal, +1 for clearing the overachieve challenge — roughly 1-2 a week if you're working
Medals no longer hand out tokens on their own; they're celebration-only now
Existing save stockpiles are recalculated once, automatically, on next load

changes: [fix] Home tiles now come from a single registry, so they can't drift out of sync with the sidebar
[redesign] Multiple Productivity tabs have been given touch-ups

_comment_tags: Changelog lines can start with a bracketed tag, e.g. "[bug] Fixed the thing".
This key is documentation only — the app never reads it, just 'version' and 'changelog' above.
[new] / [feature] / [added]                       -> New (sage)
[bug] / [fix] / [fixed] / [bugfix]                 -> Bug (red)
[security]                                         -> Security (red)
[redesign] / [redesigned]                          -> Redesign (purple)
[rework] / [reworked]                              -> Rework (amber)
[improvement] / [improved] / [perf] / [performance]-> Improved (blue)
[removed]                                          -> Removed (neutral)
[deprecated]                                       -> Deprecated (neutral)
Any other bracketed word -> still renders as a neutral pill, title-cased.
No brackets at all -> plain untagged line.
Tags are case-insensitive and only match at the very start of the line.
Each entry in 'changes' can also be an object instead of a plain string,
to break one tagged line down into specifics:
{ "text": "[fix] Tokens accumulating rapidly", "sub": ["detail one", "detail two"] }
'text' follows the same [tag] + markdown rules as a plain-string line.
'sub' is a list of plain strings, rendered as a smaller nested bullet list
underneath — each one also supports its own [tag] and markdown if needed,
though that's rarely necessary for a sub-bullet.
